'''Corey Jae Crowder''' ({{IPAc-en|dʒ|eɪ}} {{respell|JAY}};{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}} born July 6, 1990) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL]] of the French [[LNB Élite]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. Not being heavily recruited out of high school, Crowder committed to [[South Georgia Technical College]] and later [[Howard College]], where he led the team to an [[NJCAA Division I men's basketball championship|NJCAA Division I championship]] in his sophomore season. While at Howard College, Crowder was also named [[NABC Player of the Year#State Farm Junior College Player of the Year|State Farm Junior College Player of the Year]]. Later, he transferred to [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]], where he was named [[Big East Player of the Year]] in his senior season. After his senior year, Crowder declared for the [[2012 NBA draft]], where he was drafted 34th overall by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] and traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on draft night. In 2014, Crowder was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]]. He spent three years in Boston before being traded back to his draft team, the Cavaliers, in August 2017. In 2018, Crowder was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]]. He was dealt to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in 2019, and he was traded to the [[Miami Heat all-time roster|Miami Heat]] in 2020, with whom he reached his first [[NBA Finals]] with [[2020 NBA Finals|the same year]]. In the 2020 offseason, Crowder signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]] and reached his second [[NBA Finals]] in [[2021 NBA Finals|2021]]. After disagreements between Crowder and the Suns' front office, both sides mutually agreed on having Crowder sit out for the start of the [[2022–23 NBA season|2022–23 season]]. He would eventually be traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in 2023. In 2024, he signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]]. ==Early life== Jae Crowder was born on July 6, 1990, in Villa Rica, Georgia, to Helen Thompson and basketball player [[Corey Crowder]]. Crowder attended [[Villa Rica High School]], where he played as starting [[quarterback]] for the [[American football|football]] team and as starting [[point guard]] for the basketball team. Crowder spent the summer holidays in Florida, working out and training with his father, then a professional basketball player with 2 years experience in the NBA who was playing in Europe. Growing up, he was undersized and overweight, weighing nearly 200 pounds in his junior year. Eventually, he called his father to help him lose weight. By the end of his junior year, he had grown to {{convert|6|ft|4|in|m|2|abbr=on}} and had significantly improved his physical conditioning.{{Cite news |title = Out of the Shadows ... of thy Father: Jae's hardcourt journey of dreams |url = http://www.times-georgian.com/view/full_story/8814203/article-Out-of-the-Shadows---of-thy-Father--Jae-s-hardcourt-journey-of-dreams?instance=TG_sports_news |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120313135546/http://www.times-georgian.com/view/full_story/8814203/article-Out-of-the-Shadows---of-thy-Father--Jae-s-hardcourt-journey-of-dreams?instance=TG_sports_news |archive-date = March 13, 2012 |newspaper = Times Georgian |access-date = November 27, 2012 }} ==College career== Crowder was not heavily recruited out of high school, although he had some offers in football. He committed to [[South Georgia Technical College]], a college in Americus, Georgia. He later transferred to Howard College for his sophomore season. After his junior college eligibility ended, he transferred to Marquette. ===South Georgia Tech=== In his only season with South Georgia Tech, he led the Jets to their first-ever NJCAA national tournament appearance in his freshman season, under head coach Steven Wright, with the team finishing with a 21–7 record.{{cite web|title=Jae Crowder Profile|url=http://www.gomarquette.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/crowder_jae00.html|work=Marquette University Official Athletic Site|publisher=Marquette University|access-date=March 7, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160905192209/http://www.gomarquette.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/crowder_jae00.html|archive-date=September 5, 2016}} He was named [[Georgia Collegiate Athletic Association|Georgia Junior College Athletic Association Player of the Year]] that season.{{cite web|title=Marquette Lands Jae Crowder|url=http://marquette.scout.com/2/943944.html|work=Marquettehoops.com|publisher=Marquette University|date=February 3, 2010|access-date=November 27, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110311060038/http://marquette.scout.com/2/943944.html|archive-date=March 11, 2011}} ===Howard College=== In his sophomore season with the Howard Hawks in 2010, Crowder was not only named [[NABC NJCAA Player of the Year]] but also helped the team win its first-ever [[NJCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NJCAA Division I championship]]. In the final game, he registered 27 points and 12 rebounds in an 85–80 overtime victory against [[Three Rivers Community College (Missouri)|Three Rivers Community College]]. He averaged 18.9 points, 9.0 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.4 steals per game as a sophomore while shooting 46.0 percent from the field and 76.0 percent from the free throw line. ===Marquette=== After his season with the Howard Hawks, Crowder transferred to Marquette University, selecting the Golden Eagles over [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]] and [[Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball|Illinois State]], among others.
